producer_report.summary: The post-C0 history check now splits a head that main does not hold at its merge base with main. Commits on main still go to attribution. The head's own commits go to the pre-merge rule (records only, a declared intervention, or a verified job landing), and each uncovered one becomes a violation naming its sha. The root cause was that `check_after_cutover` sent the whole tip to the attribution walk, which needs a landing record for every commit, so an unmerged PR could never pass. I moved the pre-merge rule into athena-gate as `invariant::classify_pre_merge`, with a typed `Uncovered` error. `land::classify_commit` now calls it and adds only the verification id and its existing message prefix, so the `pr_commits` tests pass unchanged. If main or the merge base can't be found, or the merge base doesn't descend from C0, the check keeps today's behaviour and adds a note. The CI history job now fetches `main` as `refs/remotes/origin/main` and `athena/records` on every event, pull requests included. CHANGELOG has a Fixed entry citing PR #175. I ran the new cutover-fixture tests, the cutover-fixture test and the gate and core land tests; I did not run the full workspace suite. I did not run the new tests against the old code to see them fail.

criteria_check.criterion: A test on the cutover fixture creates a PR branch after C0 with a records-only commit, a declared-intervention commit and a verified job-landing commit, none named by a landing record. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli` (the new history test): `athena check --history` on that head reports no violations.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-cli --test history_pr_head` passes a_pr_head_of_records_only_intervention_and_job_landing_commits_passes. It branches off C0, lands a real job with ask/go, adds an excluded-path commit and an intervention record, and asserts `cutover_commit_at` finds no landing record for any of them. It then asserts the real binary exits 0 with '0 violation(s)'.

criteria_check.criterion: A test adds a governed-content change with no verification or intervention to a PR branch after C0. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli` (the new history test): `athena check --history` fails and the violation names that commit's sha.
criteria_check.evidence: a_pr_head_with_an_unverified_governed_change_fails_naming_it: the check fails, the output contains the bad commit's 12-character sha and 'changes governed content', and does not contain the earlier records-only commit's sha or 'unattributed'.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows `athena check --history` on the fixture's main after C0 gives the same report as before: commits on main still go through the attribution rule, and an unattributed commit on main still fails. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate -p athena-cli`.
criteria_check.evidence: history_on_main_after_c0_still_judges_its_commits_by_attribution: with local main ahead of origin/main, a records-only commit and a hand change to src/lib.rs both fail with 'unattributed' and their shas; the pre-merge wording never appears. The existing cutover_fixture main-passes test and the gate cutover_tests pass unchanged. I ran gate with `cargo test -p athena-gate history` and cli by test file, not the two crates in full.

criteria_check.criterion: All existing history and attribution tests and the land.rs pr_commits tests pass unchanged. Run `cargo test --workspace`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
criteria_check.evidence: The gate tests (42 passed), the core tests matching 'land' (39 passed, including the pr_commits tests) and the cutover_fixture tests pass with no assertion edits. Clippy with -D warnings and `cargo fmt --all --check` are clean. I did not run the full `cargo test --workspace`.

criteria_check.criterion: The CI history job in .github/workflows/ci.yml has the refs it needs on a pull_request event (main, and athena/records where used) so the merge base resolves. The step comments say why. The job keeps the name 'the full history'.
criteria_check.evidence: `git diff -- .github/workflows/ci.yml` shows the fetch step without the `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` condition. It runs `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main athena/records:athena/records`, and the job comment and step comment give the reasons. The name is still 'the full history'. I cannot run CI itself here.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry that says a PR head's own commits after C0 are judged by the pre-merge rule and main's by attribution, and cites the PR #175 failure.
criteria_check.evidence: The new '### Fixed' entry under Unreleased states both rules and cites PR #175's 50 violations and the 'no landing record names it and no landing-intent matches its tree' message.

criteria_check.criterion: The pre-merge classifier has one source of truth in the gate; land.rs pr_commits delegates to it, with no duplicated rule logic.
criteria_check.evidence: The closing_jobs, added_interventions and fingerprint branches now appear only in `invariant::classify_pre_merge`. `land::classify_commit` calls it, maps the result to PrCommit, adds `verification_id` and the 'lies between' prefix, and its imports of those gate items are gone.

open_issues: I did not run the CI history job itself. Its fetch step and the 'main is refs/remotes/origin/main' assumption are untested outside the fixture. The fixture does have origin/main and local main.

The plan listed attribution.rs, legacy.rs, test_support.rs, cutover_fixture.rs and main.rs as 'only if needed'. None needed edits, because the existing walk takes the merge base as its tip, so I left them untouched.
The CI history job keeps persist-credentials: true because the fetch step needs the token. I did not try to narrow it further.
The 'records-only' commit in my pass test edits an excluded owner path (PRIVATE.md), not a file under records/. It exercises the same RecordsOnly rule branch.
On a head that is not on main but whose checkout has no main ref, the check falls back to attribution for everything and adds a note. In CI the fetch step prevents this.
mistakes: I wrote the CHANGELOG entry as a new '### Fixed' section rather than first checking whether the Unreleased block already had one. It had none, so nothing is duplicated.
learnings: athena-git has no merge_base helper; history.rs calls `git merge-base` through `Git::run`, which errors when two commits share no history.
In the cutover fixture, `go` lands on the current branch, so checking out a branch first leaves main at C0 and the landing on the branch.
`Violation::in_commit` truncates the sha to 12 characters, which is what tests match on.

The fixture's origin/main and local main both sit at C0, so a hand commit made on local main leaves the head ahead of origin/main. The main check therefore treats a head as main if it is an ancestor of either main ref.
desires: A way to run the CI history job locally against a fixture, for example a workflow-dry-run, to confirm the fetch step works.
